findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There was not a CFPM available during the inspection. The PIC stated that his had lapsed and he had not re-done it yet. They were instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts that have food handling in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink nearest to the door was blocked with a trash can. The inspector moved the can in order to begin the inspection quicker and discussed the situation with the PIC later in the inspection. Education was conducted with the PIC during the inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks are readily accessible at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated that employees will sign the forms. The inspector provided blank copies to the PIC for each employee to sign. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/20/2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Food debris was observed in the handwashing sink which prevented water from draining quickly. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the food debris was removed. Ensure employees use the handwashing sink for handwashing purposes only and the sink should not be blocked with food debris to prevent water from flowing easily.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Food debris were observed on clean dishes at the dish washing area. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the dishes were placed in the dish machine. Ensure dishes are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Food processors were observed on the counter with water in them and not inverted for proper drying. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the food processors were moved to the dish rack and inverted for proper drying. Ensure utensils are stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The grate and the tray on the non-working cooler used for storing baking trays were observed to have accumulation of food residue. The PIC was instructed to have the food residue removed before the next routine inspection. Ensure the grate and tray are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink by the three-compartment sink was observed to be in need of caulking. The PIC was informed to have the handwashing sink caulked to the wall to allow for easy and smooth cleaning. Ensure the handwashing sink is caulked before the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket. CORRECTED -  The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following area were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Soil accumulation and food debris were observed at the right corner under the prep sink.
2. Under the mat at the three-compartment sink was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. In-between the wall comings under the handwashing sink at the entrance was observed to have soil accumulation.
4. Food debris and soil accumulation were observed in a large hole covered with a grate at the cook line 

The PIC was instructed to have the areas mentioned above cleaned. Ensure the facility is cleaned as often as necessary, especially hidden areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink nearest to the door was blocked with trash cans and the rolling tray carrier. The dish person moved the items prior to discussion and prior to the arrival of the PIC. Education was conducted with the PIC during his inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks are readily accessible at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

The scoop holder for the ice machine is observed with contaminants in the standing water at the bottom. The ice scoop sits in this holder consistently throughout the day. The item and contaminants were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are cleaned regularly and specifically whenever contamination has occurred.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The edge of the deflector in both ice machines is soiled and in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and had the items cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained in a clean state at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An open can of soda was observed in one of the standing coolers in the kitchen. This can is on a wire shelf over and next to foods intended for residents. The PIC was shown and removed the can to correct. Employee personal foods can be in coolers so long as they are stored in a way that removes the possibility of contaminating other foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives and pans in the kitchen are observed with remaining food debris on them as they are in storage as ready-for-use. These items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage/use. It is highly suggested that the dish washers are educated to review dishes after washing and prior to storage.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

The scoop holder for the ice machine is observed with contaminants in the standing water at the bottom. The ice scoop sits in this holder consistently throughout the day. The item and contaminants were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are cleaned regularly and specifically whenever contamination has occurred.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests.

Numerous flies are observed in the dish and hand sink areas of the kitchen. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agent (Orkin) for help in remediating the situation. A follow-up will be conducted in three weeks to allow for remediation to take affect throughout the life cycle of the flies observed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The floor in the dry storage area has dried spills and debris observed. These areas should be cleaned often enough to prevent soilage from accumulating. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple freshly washed pans on the storing racks are observed with food debris still on them. Some of the items on these racks are dry as well and also have food debris still on them. It is believed that these items are not being completely cleaned when ran through dish. The items in question were moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct the immediate violation. The PIC should educate staff to ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned between uses.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Test strips were not available for the chemical used in the dish machine during this inspection. Test strips were acquired during this inspection to correct. Ensure that test strips are available for any sanitizer used in the food areas at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket across from the stoves is observed to have a minimal change on the inspector’s test strips, indicating a concentration well below the 200 ppm needed. Bucket was remade during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds. 

The dish machine would not register CL sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility test strips. Maintenance was called but could not correct the issue. The contracted company was contacted for maintenance but did not arrive prior to the end of the inspection. Follow up is being set for Monday as the standard 3 days lands on the weekend.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Pork chops, mixed vegetables and stuffing are observed in steam wells holding between 104F-136F. It appears that the heating element for this equipment was not turned on when the foods were moved to here. The items were cooked less than an hour prior to observation. These items were moved back to the oven for reheating and the equipment turned on during this inspection. Ensure that all TCS foods are properly hot held at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

A mop is observed stored with the head in dirty mop water next to the door into the kitchen. Education was conducted with the PIC and the mop adjusted so that the head can drip dry to correct.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

1) A partially consumed water bottle is observed on a shelf across from the dish machine mixed in with cleaned dishes. 2) A partially consumer bottle of Mountain Dew is observed in a standing cooler mixed in with containers of foods intended for consumers/residents. The PIC was shown both locations and a conversation was had in relation to storage of employee foods/drinks. These items should be stored below and/or away from items intended for the residents to ensure no possible contamination. The bottles were discarded during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) The ice scoops next to the kitchen ice machine has a moist towel in the bottom of the container. PIC consulted. The towel was removed and the scoop and scoop holder moved to dish for cleaning. 2) The ice scoop holder next to the ice machine in the 300 area is observed with a soiled bottom. PIC was consulted and the items moved to dish to correct. Ensure that all food contact items are stored in a way that prevents potential contamination.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The soap dispenser at the hand sink next to the three part sink is empty during this inspection. PIC was consulted and indicated that a work order was being put in for the replacement and that it should be replaced by the end of the day. “Dennis” arrived during the inspection to replace it while inspector was still in the building to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket across from the stoves is observed to have a minimal change on the inspector’s test strips, indicating a concentration well below the 200 ppm needed. Bucket was remade during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Two green working buckets observed with no red sanitizer bucket present. Food employee was unsure which (if either) were sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Employee emptied both buckets and filled red buckets with sanitizer solution for use throughout the kitchen. Ensure chemicals are labeled to indicate what they are (or in color-coded containers, red buckets for sanitizer, green for soap is appropriate).
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Dish machine observed dispensing less than 50ppm Cl. PIC emailed maintenance personnel. Three compartment sink will be used until dish machine is verified to be sanitizing properly.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum concentration (50-200ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: A bag of sausage patties was observed to be 78F in the 2 door cooler at approximately 10:30am. PIC stated that the sausages would have been removed from hot holding at 7:30am. Food did not cool form 135F to 70F within the first two hours of the cooling process. CORRECTED— Sausage patties were voluntarily discarded. Discussed with PIC. Monitor the cooling process to ensure food achieves time/temperature requirements.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Sausage patties in the 2 door cooler observed in a pile in a sealed gallon-size ziploc bag. Sausage patties observed above 70F after 2 hours of cooling in this way. CORRECTED— Sausage patties voluntarily discarded. Discussed proper cooling methods with PIC.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
—Coving on the wall behind the stove/flat top/oven observed to be missing. Coving on the wall near the dish machine observed to be warped and pulling away from the wall. Replace/repair coving so that it creates a smooth and easily cleanable transition from wall to floor.
—The caulking around the front handsink is not smooth and creates some gaps between the caulk/handsink/wall. Seal to eliminate gaps and prevent soil accumulation.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed using clean hands to turn faucet off after washing. Use paper towel or other barrier to prevent recontamination of clean hands. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Provide education to employees.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels present at the back handwashing sink. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC, who provided paper towels. Ensure towels are always available at each handwashing sink.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Dish machine observed dispensing less than 50ppm Cl. CORRECTED— PIC discussed with maintenance personnel. Three compartment sink will be used until dish machine is verified to be sanitizing properly.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum concentration (50-200ppm). [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
-Holes observed around both kitchen handwashing sinks (left from previous paper towel dispensers). Fill holes.
-Back handwashing sink is not caulked to the wall. Seal to eliminate gap between sink and wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Open can of Coke observed on the paper towel dispenser above the dish area handsink. CORRECTED-- Discarded. Employee beverages must be in closed containers that prevent contamination of both hands and food. 
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Cream of wheat from breakfast was observed to be 63F (probed) during this inspection (after 2PM). CORRECTED-- Cream of wheat discarded. Reviewed cooling practices with staff.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Aloe vera gel observed stored on shelving near spices and baking supplies. CORRECTED-- Moved to storage in the first aid kit. 
7-208.11: (A) First aid supplies that are in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for EMPLOYEES’ shall be labeled properly (Pf). (B) Shall be stored in kit or container preventing contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (P).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Coving/trim is missing from the wall/floor junction behind the garbage disposal. Coving/trim is pulling way from the wall in other areas of the kitchen, including (but not limited to) near the mop sink room and on the wall dividing the grill from the dish area. Ensure all coving is smooth to the wall and not creating a gap.
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Can opener is not clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED- Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Clean and sanitize can opener after each use or every 4 hours during continuous use.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Scrambled eggs are 70°F (probed) and sausage patties are 66°F (probed) in the kitchen cooler. Foods began cooling after breakfast, and did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours. CORRECTED- Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled foods were voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F). (P)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Date marking is not on a gallon of milk in the kitchen cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded milk.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Single-service forks are stored with the food contact end up. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. CORRECTED- Employee with clean gloved hands rearranged utensils to reflect proper storage.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11 (B) Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and by CONSUMERS if CONSUMER self-service is provided. (C)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Food employee entered kitchen and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. CORRECTED- Discussed proper handwashing procedures with PIC and employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. (P)

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No Certified Food Manager (CFM) present at time of inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. (C)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed kitchen employee return to the kitchen and put on gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Discussed with employee, who re-washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 (H) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. (P)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed tray rack blocking the handsink near the kitchen entrance. Handsinks must always be unobstructed and easily accessible. CORRECTED- Cart was relocated.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: No employee health documentation is present at facility. All employees must have documentation at facility. Corrected. Handout provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Observed Chicken, Green Beans, and Mashed Potatoes to be approx. 80F after 3 hours. Cooling was done incorrectly. Products were discarded. Ensure proper cooling occurs for all TCS foods. Corrected. Education provided.
Food must drop from 135F to 70F in 2 hours. Within 4 hours of dropping to 70F, the food must reach 41F. The whole process can take upto 6 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Chicken, Green beans, and mashed potatoes are approx. 80F. Food did not cool from 135?F to 70?F within two hours and from 135?F to 41?F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed R-I Cooler (Cook Fridge) to be out of temperature. Air temperature was measured to be 46F. Multiple food products were discarded. These included Spaghetti Sauce, Green Beans, Chicken Salad, cut lettuce and tomatoes. All foods exceeded 41F. All TCS foods out of temp. were discarded. Corrected. PIC stated work order has been placed on unit. Unit was leaking.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41?F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41?F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed 2 containers that were soiled inside, but storing clean utensils. Ensure that the containers are properly cleaned at regular intervals to prevent contamination of clean utensils. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
1) Observed an "Arnold Palmer" stored in the freezer in the kitchen. This is wrong on two different occurences. It does not have a lid or straw, which allows for hand-to-mouth contact, thusly increasing contamination to hands. It also was stored above service foods, which is improper. Employee drinks should be stored below and away from food/food contact surfaces. 2) Observed cooked eggs stored on a shelf with other service food, but the eggs were intended for personal use and not to be reused within the facility. Ensure personal food is clearly marked if it is going to be taken home and that it is stored below and away from other service food. Drink and eggs were moved during the inspection. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the cooler on the far left, in the kitchen, to not have a guard over one of the fans. This poses a safety risk and a risk to the food if an injury were to occur. Ensure that a guard is provided for this fan to prevent injury and consequent contamination of food. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer bucket to not be at the proper concentration (<100 ppm) of quat. Upon further investigation, it was noted that the sanitizer comes out at the faucet cold and there is no way to warm the solution. The facility should contact EcoLab to determine a way to either; 1) increase the output concentration so it can be mixed with warm water for increased solubility or 2) adding a mixing valve to allow for hot water to be mixed in to create a warmed solution. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer bucket on the line that was at 100 ppm of quat. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is available and at the right concentration during hours of food preparation. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
